en: The Philippine eagle can spread its wings up to six feet wide to glide silently through the dense rainforest canopy.
National hero Jose Rizal was a polymath who could speak and write in twenty-two different languages.
The eight rays of the sun on the Philippine flag represent the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish rule.
The ancient Banaue Rice Terraces, carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people, are over two thousand years old.
Before the Spanish arrived, early Filipinos wrote on bamboo and leaves using an ancient script called Baybayin.
Dr. Fe del Mundo became the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School when she enrolled in 1936.
Bacolod’s MassKara Festival features dancers wearing giant, smiling masks originally created to lift the city's spirits during a 1980s economic crisis.
The Philippines is home to the Pearl of Lao Tzu, one of the largest natural pearls ever discovered.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution explicitly guarantees the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology.
General Emilio Aguinaldo officially proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain by waving the flag from his balcony in Kawit.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his massive Spoliarium painting.
The traditional bayanihan custom literally involved an entire community physically carrying a nipa hut to help a family relocate.
